newsitem.title: SPAIN: Opera says difficult to catch up on Retevision.
newsitem.headline: Opera says difficult to catch up on Retevision.

text.p: Consortium Opera, comprised of Spain's BCH, France Telecom and Sprint, said on Tuesday it would be very difficult to cut the distance with its competitor to acquire 60 percent of Retevision.
Opera offered some 30 percent less than that of a second group headed by Endesa and Italy's Stet, Retevision said earlier.

"The economic offer is very important to the award, and although it is not the only factor, it's going to be difficult to cut the current distance," a representative of Opera told Reuters after the two offers were officially announced.
Opera offered up to 84 billion pesetas for the initial privatisation of Retevision, while the offer from the Endesa- Stet group reached 116.36 billion pesetas.

"We went to the limit of our calculation of viability, and if another group is prepared to pay more, the future basic telephone operator will be born with a heavy weight before it becomes a profitable company," the representative said.
He added that Opera's offer seemed too high to Deutsche Telekom, which helped found Opera, but which abandoned the project in mid-May.
